A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ShowTable research. All 25 pages of v1 and 26 pages of v2, including appendices, are readable; existing equations, results, and illustrations can be matched across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original TableVisBench experiments, module and refinement-round ablations, reward-training curves, and additional Wan2.5 evaluations.

after.justification: V2 retains these original experiments and adds a code-generation baseline comparison and a human-preference study.

M1.justification: The rewriting, generation, reflection, and refinement procedure remains unchanged, including supervised rewriting training, reward-model training, GRPO refinement, and early stopping. The added experiments use configurations of existing components.

E1.justification: The training sources, creative table visualization task, and 800-instance TableVisBench remain unchanged. The added code comparison and 20-table human study address the same task without introducing documented new domains or datasets.

E2.justification: V2 newly evaluates Gemini-2.5-pro generating Python/Matplotlib plotting code against ShowTable in Table A1. Although Gemini already appeared as a pipeline component, this code-rendering comparator was absent from v1. Existing comparator sets are retained.

E3.justification: Appendix D.3 adds voting by 20 evaluators on 20 randomly selected tables, comparing three pipeline configurations across five dimensions. The code comparison also introduces a specified Gemini/Wan2.5/GPT-5 configuration. Existing benchmark metrics and training and inference settings are unchanged.

E4.justification: V2 adds human assessment of the base, rewriting-only, and full-pipeline variants, plus two qualitative code-versus-ShowTable cases in Figure A1. These provide additional component validation and examination of presentation quality; existing ablations and refinement analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental confidence intervals, significance tests, or repeated-seed uncertainty estimates. The new study reports participant and instance counts and preference percentages, without adding uncertainty estimation or statistical testing.

E6.justification: Existing Tables 1–5 and the Wan2.5 results, moved from Table A1 to A2, retain their values. New Table A1 reports code versus ShowTable overall scores of 79.4 versus 67.9 and aesthetic scores of 4.1 versus 4.9. Table A3 adds human preferences, including 73.75% for full-pipeline data accuracy; the base model leads text rendering at 38.50%.

T1.justification: The losses, GRPO objective and advantage, and benchmark score definitions are substantively unchanged. Equation 2 abbreviates the expectation notation, while Appendix Equation A1 retains its full form. No new theoretical results or proofs appear.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: creative table visualization, ShowTable, three data-construction pipelines, and TableVisBench. The added experiments support and contextualize these claims without changing their main stated scope.

C2.justification: Appendix A.1 newly acknowledges code generation's factual-accuracy advantage and explicitly excludes replacing conventional plotting when numerical precision is the sole priority. Appendix D.3 interprets human preferences and the base model's text-rendering advantage. The existing Appendix E limitations are retained.

D1.justification: New Table A1 documents Python/Matplotlib for the code baseline and specifies all four ShowTable modules used in that comparison. Existing training hyperparameters, prompts, GPU count, data-processing instructions, and project access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V2 adds references including UniLIP, CORES, Wan2.6, Nano Banana Pro, and video-generation work. Appendix A.1 sharpens positioning relative to code-based visualization. Updated GPT-5 and Qwen3-VL references concern the same previously used models.

P1.justification: Changes include localized introductory editing, expanded Appendix A.1 discussion, a new user-study subsection and acknowledgments, and revised author and supplementary-material headings. The main narrative structure is retained. The new user-study text contains an unresolved '??' table reference.

P2.justification: V2 adds the code-comparison table and figure and the human-preference table. Main Table 4 moves from page 8 to page 7, and existing appendix figures and tables are renumbered and reflowed. Most illustrations, plots, and case studies retain their content.

improvement.justification: The code comparison replaces an untested contrast in v1 with evidence exposing ShowTable's accuracy–aesthetics tradeoff, and the human study adds useful validation. The explicit qualification about precision-focused plotting improves positioning. These gains are limited by the study's 20-table scope, absent uncertainty estimates, overly strong significance wording, and broken table reference; the core method and existing evidence remain unchanged.
